category: managed time-series SQL database (Enterprise and Bring Your Own Cloud); the former self-serve QuestDB Cloud is retired

free_tier.stated: No self-serve free tier is offered. The first-party pricing/Enterprise page offers a Free Enterprise Trial and a Talk to Sales route, with production offered as self-managed Enterprise or Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC); no public per-instance price is listed.
free_tier.notes: The first-party page presents only Open Source (self-managed, Apache 2.0) and Enterprise (production, contact sales or trial); the fully managed self-serve 'QuestDB Cloud' plan is not offered as a sign-it-yourself tier.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object or storage cap is published on the first-party pricing/Enterprise page

retention.stated: unverified: no hosted-plan retention period is published on the first-party pricing/Enterprise page; Enterprise supports tiered storage with hot data plus Parquet/Iceberg on object storage and TTL-based deletion or archival.
retention.notes: TTL and downsampling are described for the Enterprise engine; no fixed hosted retention window is stated.

egress.terms: unverified: no first-party hosted egress allowance or price is published; the Enterprise tier offers tiered object storage on Amazon S3, Azure Blob or GCS queried in SQL.

interface_detail: QuestDB speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol for SQL queries and accepts InfluxDB Line Protocol for ingestion; a web SQL console is listed among the features. Enterprise adds TLS on all protocols and OAuth/OIDC SSO.
tooling: PostgreSQL drivers and psql for SQL; InfluxDB Line Protocol clients for ingest; official QuestDB clients; the self-managed Open Source build is binaries, containers and source code
chaining: A managed QuestDB deployment is reached with existing PostgreSQL tooling; the open-source QuestDB engine that the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine, or on-premises/hybrid Enterprise, is the last-resort option when no hosted self-serve plan is available.

limits.value: unverified: no published numeric limit for a hosted self-serve tier (no such tier is offered); Enterprise capacity is set by contract

binding_note: No hosted self-serve tier or numeric limit exists; the binding constraint is access: production needs a sales-led Enterprise/BYOC engagement rather than a public free allowance.

identity_cost.detail: The first-party page routes production users to Talk to Sales or a Free Enterprise Trial and describes Bring Your Own Cloud, in which the user's team deploys inside its own AWS or Azure account. No self-serve signup with email or card is published for a hosted plan.

reliability_note: The former self-serve managed QuestDB Cloud is not offered on the first-party pricing page; production is a sales-led Enterprise or BYOC engagement with 99.9% uptime and SLA-backed support. The Open Source edition has basic auth over unencrypted transmission and community-only support.
confidence_note: The first-party QuestDB pricing/Enterprise page was captured on 2026-11-19; it lists only Open Source and Enterprise/BYOC with a sales and trial route and no hosted self-serve price. No hosted numeric limits are published, so those fields are unverified.
